titleEn: Śāntiḥ three times: peace from fate, from other beings, and from your own body and mind.
meaningEn: Peace, peace, peace. The Upaniṣads end every peace-chant with the word said three times. Tradition says why: trouble reaches a person from three directions — from what no one controls (storm, accident, fate), from other living beings, and from one's own body and mind. One śāntiḥ for each. No text fixes which śāntiḥ is which; the three-fold reading itself is the commentators'.
meaningHi: शांति, शांति, शांति। उपनिषद हर शांति-पाठ को यह शब्द तीन बार कहकर पूरा करते हैं। परंपरा बताती है क्यों: दुख आदमी तक तीन तरफ़ से आता है — उससे जो किसी के बस में नहीं (आँधी, हादसा, किस्मत), दूसरे जीवों से, और अपने शरीर और मन से। हर एक के लिए एक शांति। कौन-सी शांति किसके लिए, यह कोई ग्रंथ तय नहीं करता; तीन का यह हिसाब भी टीकाकारों का है।
sayItLike: Om shaan-tih · shaan-tih · shaan-tih — a soft breath after each 'tih'

words.grammar: the -ḥ (visarga) is a soft breath after the i; tradition: ādhidaivika — trouble from the gods, the elements, chance
tradition: ādhibhautika — trouble from other creatures and people

words.glossEn: peace — from what is inside: one's own body and mind
words.glossHi: शांति — अंदर से: अपने शरीर और मन से
words.grammar: tradition: ādhyātmika — the trouble that is one's own. Which śāntiḥ is which is not fixed by any text

source.text: The closing formula of every Vedic peace-chant (śānti-pāṭha) — e.g. the Īśa, Kaṭha and Taittirīya Upaniṣads
source.ref: oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ closes the śānti-pāṭha of each Upaniṣad; the three-troubles reading is an old commentarial reading (Sāṃkhya-kārikā 1 onward)
source.note: The chant itself is Vedic and everywhere. The three-times reading (ādhyātmika, ādhibhautika, ādhidaivika) is an old commentarial reading (Sāṃkhya-kārikā 1 onward), not stated in the Upaniṣads — near-universal, and labelled here as tradition. No text fixes which śāntiḥ answers which trouble.

significance.textSays: Every Upaniṣad's peace-chant ends 'oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ' — peace, said three times, and nothing else.
significance.traditionSays: One for each of the three sources of trouble — the powers beyond anyone's hand, other beings, the self; the word that closes every Upaniṣad.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That saying it brings peace. It asks for peace, three ways; that is all the word does.
